policy.rule: Documented phonological plausibility is not automatic cognacy or a universal sound law.

new_support: Merrill et al. 2020 documents historical e~i and é~í alternations: síneví~síniví, taitéke~taitéki, ¢elé~¢elí.
Merrill cautions that vowel alternations are limited and show no evident general pattern.
SEP catalogs Awilichi bawi as a Rarámuri publication from Chihuahua; an indexed textual reproduction preserves Echi nise’ami and repeated niseami in a goat-herding narrative.
candidates.supports: The Nessé~Nisé vowel difference is non-ad-hoc and phonologically plausible; pastoral semantic/derivational convergence is reinforced.
candidates.does_not_support: Automatic cognacy, a regular e>i law, or a universal -ameke>-ami pathway.
candidates.next_source_test: Recover the care/herd/shepherd family in an independently identified modern variety, ideally Hilton et al. 1993 or the 2016 Samachique update.

candidates.supports: Strong same-root extension variation in Tellechea's historical ame domain.
candidates.does_not_support: A participial-specific deletion mechanism. Tellechea's explicit que/ca deletion statement concerns preterites.

candidates.reason: Merrill documents the alternations but says they are limited and lack an evident pattern; they establish plausibility, not lexical identity.

global_constraints: No universal e > i or é > í law.
No automatic cognacy from a phonological alternation documented in other lexemes.
No automatic transfer of Tellechea preterite que/ca deletion to participles.
